name: c3bot-relay
description: c3bot-relay (#1579): Telegram <-> c3 relay on a dedicated bot (Bot B). One inbound Telegram long-poll fans out to c3 clients over three transports: WebSocket (/ws, full duplex), Server-Sent Events (/events, Last-Event-ID resume) and long-poll (/poll, cursor). Outbound via POST /send or a WS send frame. Zero npm dependencies. Bearer-gated, mesh-only.

primary._auth_doc: auth none: the app gates every call itself with its own bearer (C3BOT_RELAY_TOKEN, 401 without it; /health is open). The fleet forward_auth would reject this token and buffer SSE; the route stays WG-only. streaming:true keeps SSE and WebSocket unbuffered.

api.description: Telegram <-> c3 relay: WS /ws, SSE /events, long-poll /poll, POST /send.

secrets._doc: Two secrets by NAME, values only in the private vault at Linux-Containers/infra-api_c3bot-relay/src/secrets.yaml (the vault keeps the pre-#1483 dir; _rebrand-1450/vault-dir-renames.txt maps it to this dir) (sops, public fleet recipient); the Ship overlay copies it in and the engine mounts .secrets (env_file). C3BOT_RELAY_TOKEN: 64-hex bearer of the relay API (CI sops-create generates it); the server exits 78 when empty. C3BOT_RELAY_BOT_TOKEN: the Telegram bot token of the DEDICATED relay bot (Bot B, minted in @BotFather by the owner). It must NOT be C3_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: cloud-infra-mcp long-polls that token and Telegram answers 409 to a second getUpdates consumer. While the bot token is absent the relay still starts and serves all three transports; /health reports telegram:'unconfigured' and /send answers 503.
